No claim is a mandatory step before another. Consumer law lets you choose between demanding performance, accepting something equivalent or undoing the contract. <1><2>p. 540</2></1>

It may involve maintaining or restoring access, reversing or reviewing sanctions, preserving history, reactivating functionalities, substitution by a functionally equivalent position, reversibility of versions when technically possible, procedural corrections of governance, duties of verifiable reasoning, intelligible mechanisms of challenge and other means able to re-establish, substantially, the utility legitimately incorporated into the relationship.<1>p. 740</1>

Hence the importance of art. 35 of the CDC<1><2>1</2></1>, which allows demanding specific performance of the obligation, accepting an equivalent performance or rescinding the contract with losses and damages<3>p. 540</3>

Preservation of evidence and production of documents
Dynamic allocation of the burden, under art. 373 of the CPC<1><2>4</2></1>
The more reconstruction depends on internal governance, the less the consumer can be required to provide what was never within reach. <1><2>p. 736</2></1>

The third mechanism is procedural and brings together preservation of evidence, production of documents and dynamic redistribution of the burden. Art. 373, § 1, of the CPC<1><2>5</2></1> allows the judge to assign the burden differently in the cases provided by law or in view of peculiarities of the case related to the impossibility or excessive difficulty of meeting the burden, or to the greater ease of obtaining proof of the contrary fact, provided by a reasoned decision. This is the normal configuration of disputes over IOCs, in which logs, interface trails, change histories, sanction criteria and internal support communications are concentrated in the supplier, and redistribution appears, with support from the manual by Benjamin, Marques and Bessa, as the technically adequate response to the structural asymmetry of proof.

The most direct route to operate open auditability is the production of a document or thing under arts. 396 to 400 of the CPC<1><2>6</2></1>. Art. 396 of the CPC<3><4>7</4></3> authorises the judge to order the production of a document or thing in a party's possession, and art. 397 of the CPC<5><6>8</6></5> requires the request to identify the document as completely as possible, the purpose of the proof and the circumstances indicating that it exists and is held by the opposing party. Hence the rule, surgical requests and not procedural fishing expeditions. Instead of all the system's data, the consumer can request the history of relevant versions of a given item, the trail of screens shown at purchase, the minimum records of the specific transaction, the content of the change notice or the category and reason of the sanction applied.

Likewise, the regime for the production of a document or thing provided for in arts. 396 to 400 of the CPC<1><2>6</2></1> offers the most direct route to make open auditability operational.<3>p. 659</3>

If the supplier denies holding the document, art. 398 of the CPC<1><2>9</2></1> allows the requesting party to prove, by any means, that the statement is untrue. Under art. 399 of the CPC<3><4>10</4></3>, refusal is not admitted if the respondent has a legal obligation to produce it, if it referred to the document in the proceedings to build its case or if the document is common to the parties. In the face of an unjustified refusal, art. 400 of the CPC<5><6>11</6></5> authorises the judge to accept as true the facts the document would serve to prove. These are the guarantees that answer the formulas platform litigation knows well, such as that the information no longer exists, that it is internal-use data or that there is no way to reconstruct the procedure.

The reference provision is art. 6, VIII, of the CDC<1><2>12</2></1>, which ensures that the defence of consumer rights is facilitated, including through reversal of the burden of proof. The disagreement lies in how to apply the guarantee to the digital environment. Mariana de Moraes Palmeira, starting from digital vulnerability, argues for the universalisation of the consumer's hyposufficiency in that environment and, by derivation, for reversal of the burden as a rule, ope legis, that is, by force of the law itself, and not only ope judicis, by the judge's decision in the case. The gain is real, a concrete protective response above all in matters of proof, but it has a limit, because the consequence is organised as a block, from an overall perception of a hostile environment, without isolating the specific mechanism that produces the asymmetry. The alternative is to move the basis to the mechanism, and then proof comes to require preservation of trails, verifiable transparency and rational redistribution of the burden.

On one point the CDC itself already allocates the burden. Art. 38 of the CDC<1><2>13</2></1> assigns to whoever sponsors the advertising information or communication the burden of proving its truthfulness and correctness, and in this lies the normative recognition that advertising is a space of power and responsibility. In IOCs, the provision prevents the consumer from having to prove alone that the expectation produced by the communication was incompatible with the actual regime of enjoyment.
